report_name: FCC Mandates Cybersecurity Overhaul for U.S. Emergency Alert System

threat_actors.name: EAS Hijackers
threat_actors.description: Unspecified threat actors who have successfully compromised internet-connected Emergency Alert System (EAS) equipment to broadcast false alerts, as mentioned in the FCC report. This entity represents the criminals and potential foreign adversaries cited as the reason for the new FCC rule.
threat_actors.goals: Broadcast false and alarming messages to cause panic or disruption.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors compromised internet-connected Emergency Alert System (EAS) equipment to broadcast false alerts.

attack_patterns.name: Default Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers leveraged default credentials on EAS equipment to gain unauthorized access. The FCC's new rule explicitly prohibits default passwords in response to these attacks.

identities.name: Federal Communications Commission
identities.description: U.S. government agency that adopted a final rule to mandate cybersecurity measures for the Emergency Alert System (EAS).

identities.name: EAS Participants
identities.description: A class of organizations including broadcasters, cable providers, and satellite radio services that are required to comply with the new FCC cybersecurity rules for the Emergency Alert System.

identities.name: Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau
identities.description: A bureau of the FCC that previously issued advisories on EAS security and whose guidance is now codified into a final rule.

infrastructure.name: Internet-Connected EAS Equipment
infrastructure.description: Internet-facing Emergency Alert System (EAS) equipment that was compromised by attackers to broadcast false alerts. The new FCC rule mandates firewalls to protect this infrastructure.

indicators.name: EAS DASDEC Process Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: EAS DASDEC Process Execution
id: 9c7d1e8f-a3b4-4c6d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of the 'dasdec' process, which is associated with Emergency Alert System (EAS) equipment. Execution on non-EAS systems or by unexpected users could indicate compromise.
references:
  - https://www.fcc.gov
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-01
tags:
  - attack.t1190
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/dasdec'
    OriginalFileName:
      - 'dasdec'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate execution on authorized EAS encoder/decoder systems.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the 'dasdec' process, a key component of some EAS equipment. This could indicate activity on a compromised EAS device.

indicators.name: EAS DASDEC Web Interface Access
indicators.pattern:
title: EAS DASDEC Web Interface Access
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests to the common management interface path for DASDEC Emergency Alert System (EAS) equipment. This could indicate scanning or an attempt to exploit a public-facing device.
references:
  - https://www.fcc.gov
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-01
tags:
  - attack.t1190
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains:
      - '/dasdec/index.html'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative access to the EAS device web interface.
indicators.description: Detects access to the '/dasdec/index.html' URL path, which is a common attack surface for internet-exposed EAS equipment.
